subject: ACME renewal: usage review & expansion next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Barnes <julia.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 16:22:00 -0800
Subject: ACME renewal: usage review & expansion next steps

Hi Julia / Tom \u0014

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from my side so we’re aligned and can move toward a clean renewal + expansion:\u2028

Summary of current state:
- Q4 2026 avg monthly inference tokens: ~320B (mostly chat/generation workloads).
- Peak concurrency: ~220 rps for customer-facing chat service; p95 latency target currently 320ms.
- You’ve adopted embeddings for search in a few pilots (~15M embeddings/month).

Pain points you flagged:
1) Cost volatility on burst traffic \u0014 need more predictable unit economics.
2) Occasional latency spikes during EMEA peak window (routing + burst autoscale).
3) Need better ops visibility for usage and prompt-level debugging for the search pilot.

Goals we discussed:
- Renew existing contract for 2027 with a baseline reserved capacity to stabilize unit cost.
- Add a Dedicated pool for embeddings/search pilots and standardize routing to reduce p95 latency.
- Formalize an expansion plan (timeline below) for productionizing search and adding reranking.

Recommended next steps / timeline:
- I’ll share an updated pricing proposal (attached proposed_pricing_v2.pdf) that includes a dedicated GPU pool and a blended unit price for embeddings. (Deliverable: Marissa \u0014 today)
- ACME to confirm target reserved capacity (tokens/month + embeddings qps) by 2027-01-22. (Deliverable: Julia)
- Once capacity numbers are confirmed, we’ll generate a scoped SOW + updated contract and route to legal \u0014 target signature by 2027-02-28. (Owner: Marissa)
- Technical kickoff with Monica (CS) and Rishi (Solutions) to scope migration to Dedicated and routing policy changes \u0014 target week of 2027-02-07.

Attachments: ACME_usage_report_Q4_2026.csv (usage by service + p95/p99 latency), proposed_pricing_v2.pdf (pricing + options).

Open questions I noted:
- For the embeddings workload, do you expect synchronous or async inference at scale? (affects pool sizing)
- Any contractual constraints around data residency or audit logs beyond standard SOC2?

Thanks \u0014 if I missed anything, flag it and I’ll update. Happy to hop on a 15-min follow-up if helpful.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
Schedule: https://calendly.com/marissa-redwood/15

Date: Sat, 16 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Re: ACME renewal: usage review & expansion next steps

Marissa \u0014

Thanks for the thorough recap and for the attachments. Quick responses inline:\u2028

- Embeddings workload: initial phase will be async (batch embeddings for 1M rows/day) but we expect to move to near-sync for UI search by Q3 once latency is tightened. Plan for mixed mode.
- Data residency: we need logs retained 2 years and an audit trail for admin actions (SOC2 plus extra logging). I’ll confirm exact language from Legal, but please assume we need the 2-year retention.

We’re comfortable with the proposed direction; the cost numbers look reasonable pending one ask on discounts (see below). Next steps from our side:
- I’ll confirm proposed reserved capacity numbers after I sync with Tom \u0014 target EOD Friday 1/22.
- Can you outline the embedding pool sizing assumptions that led to the pricing in the PDF? I want to share that with our infra team.

Ask on discounting: we’re evaluating a three-year commit vs 1-year \u0014 curious if Redwood offers a progressive discount for multi-year or additional volume tiers. If we do 3-year commit and expand embeddings to full production in 6 months, would that be eligible for improved rates?

Appreciate it \u0014 Julia

Julia Barnes
Director, Product \u2014 Search & AI, ACME Corp
julia.barnes@acme.com | +1 (617) 555-0987
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Julia Barnes <julia.barnes@acme.com>
Cc: Tom O'Neill <tom.oneill@acme.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME renewal: usage review & expansion next steps

Julia \u0014 thanks, good clarifications. A few updates and answers below.

1) Embedding pool assumptions (high level):
- Proposal assumes mixed-mode: baseline async batch capacity for 1.2M embeddings/day, with burst headroom to support ~150 qps for near-sync search.
- GPU profile: 4x A10g-equivalent instances in Dedicated pool for embeddings, autoscale to 8 during peak; storage for KV cache sized at 2TB for vector index snapshots.
- We included a buffer for 20% month-over-month growth in the first 3 months.

2) Discounts / multi-year pricing:
- We can provide progressive discounts for committed spend: 1-year = standard, 2-year = 7% discount, 3-year = 12% discount on baseline reserved capacity.
- If ACME expands embeddings to production within 6 months and crosses the next volume tier, we’ll honor the next-tier blended rate retroactively for the term.
- I attached proposed_pricing_v2.pdf with those tiers called out (see page 2).

3) Data residency & audit logs: Monica \u0014 can you confirm we can commit to 2 year log retention + admin audit trail for this account (and any incremental cost)?

Next actions:
- Julia to confirm capacity by 2027-01-22.
- Once confirmed, I’ll produce an SOW and draft term sheet for legal review \u0014 aim for routing week of 2027-01-25.
- Schedule technical kickoff week of 2027-02-07 (Monica to lead).

If that all sounds right I’ll lock the pricing doc and start the SOW.

Best,

Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123
